fields.meta_title: What Is a Splash Page? Examples and Uses | Emergent
fields.meta_description: A splash page is the screen a site shows before its home page. See four working types, Google's mobile rule and how to build yours.
fields.h1: Build a Splash Page With a Clear Way In
fields.hero_description: Build a splash page that asks one question, shows a clear way past it, and saves each answer to a table you own.
fields.features_heading: What Goes Into a Splash Page That Works
fields.features_subheading: One screen up front, and the routing and storage behind it that visitors never see.
fields.feature_1:
A skip link placed where people look

Ask for a skip link and Emergent sets it beside the main button, as large as the button label. Visitors headed for the home page reach it in one click, with no close icon to find.
fields.feature_2:
Inner links that bypass the splash

Put the splash page at your root address and move the home page one step behind it, to a path such as /home. Links shared to a product or an article can open that page directly.
fields.feature_3:
Signups saved to a table you own

Emails typed into the splash land in a database table you own, with a timestamp and the campaign in the link. Export the list, or send each new row to your email tool over its API.
fields.feature_4:
Routing rules written in plain words

Answers about age or country send each visitor to a different page: the store for their country, or a short exit page for anyone under the age you set. Rules read as plain sentences.
fields.feature_5:
Promotions changed by message

Change the headline or end a promotion by sending Emergent a message. The new version replaces the old one at the same address, and answers already saved stay as they were.
fields.feature_6:
The page and its data, exported

The splash page and its table export to your GitHub on paid plans. Host both on Emergent under a custom domain, which is included and uses credits, or deploy the code yourself.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Jobs a Splash Page Does Well
fields.tab_content_1:
Twenty-one or older, asked at the door

Copperline Brewing's site opens on one question: are you 21 or older? Yes leads to the taproom menu and the bottle shop. No leads to a short page with the brewery's address and nothing to buy. Regulars who answered Yes skip the question for 30 days.
fields.tab_content_2:
A storefront and a language, picked once

Shoppers from three countries reach Northwind's store, and prices and shipping differ in each. The splash page asks for a country and a language, then opens the matching store. A shopper in Montreal who picks Canada and French lands on the French Canadian store and goes straight there on every later visit.
fields.tab_content_3:
Collect launch emails before the app opens

Until launch day, Lumen's domain shows one screen with a single field for an email address, under a sentence on what the app does. Each signup lands as a row with its time and the campaign that sent it. On launch day the splash comes down and the home page takes over the address.
fields.tab_content_4:
How many shoppers took the sale and how many skipped

For the first two weeks of October, Harbor Supply opens its site on a fall sale splash page. Each visitor sees it on the first visit, and later visits open on the home page. The log records whether each viewer chose Shop the sale or Skip to site, and a Slack post at 8 AM gives the marketing team yesterday's totals.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Splash Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a splash page that asks for one decision, remembers it, and lets visitors through to the site.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Name the one job it does
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Check it against Google's mobile rule
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down what the splash page is for before designing it: an age check, a storefront choice, a waitlist, or a short promotion. If you cannot name the job in a sentence, the message belongs in a banner on the home page instead.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Two buttons, or one field and a button, is enough for the screen. Each extra field or link is another reason for a visitor to leave before reaching the site they came for. Cut the navigation menu and the footer too.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Place the skip link near the main button, in readable type and plain words such as Continue to site. Tiny close icons and countdown timers that hold people in place cost you the visitors who came for the home page.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Google may rank a page lower on mobile when an intrusive interstitial hides its content. Age checks and cookie notices that answer a legal obligation are exempt. A promotional splash belongs on its own URL with a clear way through, never layered over the page someone searched for.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Store each answer in a cookie with an expiry that fits the job: weeks for an age check, months for a language. Without it, a returning customer meets the same question on every visit, and the site looks as if it has never seen them.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Keep every answer in a table
fields.howto_step_6_des: When the splash asks for an email or a country, write each answer to a table with the time and the link the visitor arrived from. That table becomes your waitlist, and later the record of which campaign filled it.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Watch the skip rate, then retire it
fields.howto_step_7_des: Compare clicks on the main button with skips and exits. A promotion most people skip is a banner's job. When the splash has done its work, take it down and point its address at the home page with a 301 redirect.

plan.angle: The top 10 is definitions (Wikipedia, Unbounce, Wix, Instapage, ActiveCampaign) and galleries (Dribbble, Mailchimp, Webflow, Landingi). They define the term and show screenshots, but few say when a splash page earns its place, how to keep it out of Google's intrusive-interstitial trouble, or what happens to the answer a visitor gives. This page defines it up top for the AI Overview, covers the comics meaning in the FAQ, and shows four working splash pages by job, each with a way past it and the visitor's choice stored.
tab_stories: Copperline Brewing's site opens on an age check that asks whether the visitor is 21 or older, sends a No to a polite exit page and remembers a Yes for 30 days.

Northwind ships to three countries, so its splash page asks for a storefront and a language once and sends a French-speaking visitor in Canada straight to the French Canadian store on every later visit.
Before Lumen's app opens to the public, its domain shows a waitlist splash page whose only field is an email address, and each signup lands as a row with the campaign that sent it.
Harbor Supply runs a fall sale splash page that each visitor sees once, logs every view, sale click and skip, and posts yesterday's numbers to the marketing team in Slack each morning.

claims_to_source: A splash page is a page shown before a website's home page, used for things such as a promotion, a language choice or an age check
In comics, a splash page is a full-page illustration, often the opening page of a story
Google may rank pages lower on mobile when an intrusive interstitial blocks the content, with exceptions for legally required ones such as age verification and cookie notices
The minimum legal drinking age in the United States is 21
Mobile apps show a splash screen with the app icon while the app loads

scope.evidence: H1 "Build a Splash Page With a Clear Way In", meta "What Is a Splash Page? Examples and Uses | Emergent" and hero "Build a splash page that asks one question, shows a clear way past it, and saves each answer to a table you own." state the whole job and stay off the one page website and microsite siblings. D1/D2 pass (QC 0).

intent.evidence: SERP is definitions and galleries with an AI Overview (AMBER, mixed meanings): FAQ 1 defines it, FAQ 3, 4 and 10 cover the landing page and home page comparisons, FAQ 5 and 8 give examples, FAQ 6 covers the comics meaning, the tabs show four working types and step 4 delivers the meta's "Google's mobile rule" ("Age checks and cookie notices that answer a legal obligation are exempt").

specificity.evidence: Splash-specific detail: "Regulars who answered Yes skip the question for 30 days", "move the home page one step behind it, to a path such as /home", "point its address at the home page with a 301 redirect". Emergent build cell is the hub default (note).

openers.evidence: "Ask for a skip link and Emergent sets it beside the main button", "Put the splash page at your root address", "Copperline Brewing's site opens on one question", "Until launch day, Lumen's domain shows one screen": full sentences, varied.

craft.evidence: QC Q2/Q5/Q6/Q7 clean; one idea per sentence ("Cut the navigation menu and the footer too."). Repeats and soft generalizations are notes.

voice.evidence: Concrete: "No leads to a short page with the brewery's address and nothing to buy", "A shopper in Montreal who picks Canada and French lands on the French Canadian store". No AI-tell vocabulary.

truth.evidence: claims_used approved; GitHub export "on paid plans"; custom domain "included and uses credits". Definition, comics meaning, intrusive-interstitial rule with legal exemptions, US drinking age 21 and app splash screens each map to domain_sources. uc-4 adds up on every row (455 = 140 + 315 through 612 = 204 + 408) and the Slack post matches Oct 7.

distinct.evidence: Pages after an action go to the thank you page (FAQ 9) and single campaigns to the event landing page (FAQ 10); the page's ground is the screen in front of a whole site.

faq.evidence: Exactly 10 items, none names a brand or asks for a file (PA14/PA15); the comics item answers a meaning the SERP itself carries for this query; answer-first; hub link in item 2; thank-you-page and event-landing-page links; moat lines in items 3, 7, 9 from approved claims.

images.evidence: uc-1 "Are you 21 or older?", Yes opens the taproom menu, "Remembered for 30 days", No opens an exit page; uc-2 three countries, Canada + French to the French Canadian store, next visit straight there; uc-3 one email field, row with spring-newsletter campaign and time; uc-4 daily log with views, sale clicks and skips, 8 AM Slack post to #marketing. Reserved domains only.
